description:
**Accepting a talk makes it disappear from the "Accepted" filter.** Operator, live
site 2026-08-11: *"I just manually accepted a talk and then I went and searched for
accepted talks and it didn't appear. That's a big one."*

They are right, and it is not a caching bug. It is the definition of "Accepted".

## Root cause

`src/routes/submissions.queries.ts:106-116`:

    function acceptedStagePredicate(submission, agenda, includeCancelledAt) {
      return `${submission}.status = 'accepted'
        AND ${agenda}.id IS NULL
        AND NOT (${onboardingStagePredicate(...)})
        AND NOT (${pendingWavePredicate(submission)})`;
    }

"Accepted" in the status dropdown does not mean *this was accepted*. It means
*accepted **and** not scheduled **and** not in onboarding **and** not in a pending
wave* — a **transient pipeline stage**, not a fact about the record.

Accepting a submission immediately gives it a pending wave, or auto-assigns speaker
tasks (`auto_assign` is set on templates in `scripts/seed/event.ts:339-360`). Either
one makes `pendingWavePredicate` or `onboardingStagePredicate` true, so the record
reclassifies to **Waved** or **Onboarding** the instant it is accepted and drops out
of "Accepted". The operator did exactly the right thing and the product lost the record.

This also explains their second observation — *"it looks like we have no accepted
statuses"*. Almost nothing ever rests in that bucket.

## The dropdown is three vocabularies wearing one label

`STATUS_OPTIONS` (`src/ui/submissions/SubmissionsPage.tsx:54-69`) is a flat list of
14 entries mixing:

- **Real statuses** (a stored fact): Draft, Submitted, Rejected, Withdrawn
- **Mutually-exclusive pipeline stages** (derived, transient): Unreviewed, Waved,
  Onboarding, Accepted, Scheduled, Published
- **A derived queue**: Decided · not notified

Operator: *"it's just like a long list. I don't know if there's anything we can do
there."* The length is a symptom; the category confusion is the disease. An organizer
reads "Accepted" as "talks I accepted" and is simply right to.

## Required outcome

**Non-negotiable:** after an organizer accepts a submission, filtering for accepted
talks finds it. Immediately, and at every later stage of its life.

How you get there is yours to choose, but state the choice and its reasoning in the
PR. The two credible shapes:

- **Status and stage become separate dimensions.** "Accepted" filters on the stored
  fact (`s.status = 'accepted'`) and matches regardless of wave/onboarding/schedule;
  pipeline stage becomes its own control. Truest to how an organizer thinks, and it
  shortens the status list on its own.
- **Keep the exclusive stages but stop mislabelling them.** Group the dropdown under
  headings (`<optgroup>`) that name what each group is, and add an explicit
  "Accepted (any stage)" entry that means the fact. Smaller change, keeps the
  existing derivation intact.

Whichever you pick:

- **Do not break MRQ-76's guarantee.** That ticket unified stage derivation so a
  dashboard tile cannot count a different set than its destination
  (`submissions.queries.ts:118-120`). Every surface consuming these predicates —
  dashboard tiles, saved views, the program board, the agenda builder — must still
  agree after your change. Find the consumers before you edit; there are several.
- **Visual treatment of the control is in scope** (operator asked): "All statuses"
  should read as the neutral default rather than one item among fourteen, and the
  list should be scannable. Grouping and a distinct treatment for the default beat
  a longer list.
- Keep the organizer's language, per `PHILOSOPHY.md`. "Maybe" is the product's word
  for waitlisted and stays.

## Ownership boundary — read this

Another delegator (**MRQ-98**) is concurrently working on the *presentation and
performance* of this same page: loading jank, the search field, the placeholder
count, saved-view discoverability.

- **You own:** `src/routes/submissions.queries.ts`, the `STATUS_OPTIONS` constant,
  the status `<select>` and its styling, and any consumer you must update for
  consistency.
- **You do not own:** the search field, the loading/skeleton behavior, the saved-view
  strip, or the toolbar layout.
- Work in your own git worktree (`git worktree add ../Marquee-worktrees/<branch> <branch>`).
  Coordinate through a Lattice comment if you truly must cross the line.

## Acceptance

- Accept a submission, then filter for accepted talks: **it is there.** Verify at
  each stage — freshly accepted, wave pending, onboarding tasks open, scheduled,
  published.
- A test covers accept-then-filter end to end. This defect was invisible to a green
  suite; do not leave it that way.
- Dashboard tiles, saved views, and the program board still agree with the list
  after the change (MRQ-76's invariant holds).
- The status control reads as categories, not a flat 14-item list, and "All statuses"
  is visibly the default.
- No status is silently dropped from the vocabulary without saying so in the PR.
- Validated **locally** with browser automation (no auto-deploy on this project —
  see `DEPLOY.md`; do not run `wrangler deploy`), screenshot in the PR.
- `npm test` green within budget; PR open against `Stage-11-Agentics/marquee` `main`.
title: Accepting a talk removes it from the Accepted filter — "Accepted" is a transient stage masquerading as a status
